stories.summary: Ubisoft is reportedly among multiple suitors preparing bids to try and purchase French developer Arkane Lyon, makers of the Dishonored series and the upcoming Marvel's Blade, from Microsoft in the wake of the first-party publisher's ongoing Xbox "reset."

sources.name: IGN
sources.title: Ubisoft Among Suitors Trying to Buy Marvel's Blade, Dishonored Studio Arkane Lyon from Xbox
sources.text: Ubisoft is reportedly among multiple suitors preparing bids to try and purchase French developer Arkane Lyon, makers of the Dishonored series and the upcoming Marvel's Blade, from Microsoft in the wake of the first-party publisher's ongoing Xbox " reset ." According to a new report from Bloomberg, at least three companies have submitted bids to Microsoft so far, with Assassin's Creed publisher Ubisoft among them. The identities of the other bidders are not yet publicly known, but Microsoft has not accepted any bids yet. Bloomberg states that a deal would allow Arkane Lyon to complete its current project, Marvel's Blade, which the outlet says "is expected to be released within the next year or two." Arkane's other studio in Austin, Texas, was closed by Microsoft in 2024 as part of a larger series of project cuts and personnel layoffs. The Austin team had been responsible for the critically acclaimed studio's only flop, 2023's disappointing co-op vampire-hunting game Redfall, which IGN gave a 4 out of 10 in our review . Previously, Arkane Austin developed the buggy-at-launch-but-quickly-fixed immersive sim Prey as well as the beloved original Dishonored. Arkane Lyon, meanwhile, was responsible for the 10-out-of-10 first-person immersive sim Deathloop along with the outstanding Dishonored 2. Four studios have been spun out of Xbox so far rather than being immediately shut down as part of the "reset": Double Fine, which has gone independent ; Compulsion Games, which has also gone independent ; Undead Labs, which has gone independent but signed a publishing deal with an unidentified company for State of Decay 3; and Ninja Theory, which unfortunately might close down after Microsoft had two deals for another company to acquire it fall through . sources.text: A new report suggests that Arkane Lyon could go indie, or be bought by Ubisoft Ubisoft has reportedly put in a bid to acquire Dishonored and Deathloop studio Arkane Lyon from Xbox. This is according to Jason Schreier of Bloomberg , who reports that several companies have put in bids to buy the Dishonored developer. The only company named in the report is Ubisoft , but Schreier reports that “at least two other gaming companies” have put in their own bids. The sale of Arkane comes as part of Xbox ‘s ongoing “reset” under CEO Asha Sharma . This has seen mass layoffs throughout Xbox, and some studios either merging, slimming down, or being spun off. According to Bloomberg, Arkane could also be among the latter, as it’s further claimed that Xbox is considering selling Arkane to its own management. This would make the studio independent, much like Double Fine and Compulsion Games . SCOOP: Several companies have made offers to buy Dishonored developer Arkane Lyon from Xbox, including Ubisoft Entertainment, according to people familiar with the negotiations www.bloomberg.com/news/article... If this report is accurate, then Arkane could still release Marvel’s Blade, which was announced in 2023. The game’s future remains uncertain while Xbox seeks to turn the studio over to new owners. It is also unclear what will become of Arkane’s other IPs, including Dishonored and Deathloop , should it be sold, although Xbox has allowed other studios to hold onto theirs. Considering Ubisoft’s own restructuring in recent months, many will be fearful of what this bid would mean for Arkane. Ubisoft-owned studios have faced a steady stream of layoffs, with multiple projects cancelled , including a Prince of Persia remake that appeared to be close to launch. However, Arkane’s prospects as an independent studio might not be much brighter, given the issues that many are running into to try and secure project funding. In fact, after going independent, Double Fine rolled out layoffs of its own . While we wait to hear what fate befalls Arkane, Ninja Theory is also trying to secure a buyer. Last month, it was reported that layoffs had begun , as two separate deals to save the studio had fallen through.

sources.text: Months after Microsoft announced that Arkane , maker of Dishonored and Deathloop , would be among the studios it is divesting as part of Xbox’s current “reset,” the tech giant still hasn’t been able to settle on a buyer. Ubisoft is among the companies currently interested in buying the studio and potentially helping it complete work on Marvel’s Blade . According to a new report by Bloomberg , the Assassin’s Creed publisher is among those currently in talks for a potential deal, having already submitted a bid. Microsoft is also reportedly exploring a sale of the studio back to its management. If no deal can be reached, a total studio closure is on the table. The terms of the proposals are unknown. A spokesperson for Microsoft told Bloomberg it continues to explore options ahead of a December deadline for a decision. Ubisoft and Arkane are both based in France, and it wouldn’t be the first time the publisher has worked on a Disney-owned license. It released Star Wars Outlaws in 2024, a game that seemingly failed to meet sales expectations despite being generally quite good. The French publisher is facing its own headwinds, however. Ubisoft has seen ongoing layoffs and restructurings as it deals with revenue shortfalls and debt payments following big production delays. Despite employing over 15,000 people, it has no major blockbuster releases coming out this fall. Last month, Microsoft revealed it had extended Arkane’s deadline for finding a potential buyer. sources.text: I'm trying to imagine a Ubisoft logo on Dishonored 3 Ubisoft and at least two other companies have reportedly offered to buy Dishonored and Marvel's Blade dev Arkane Studios from Microsoft as the company seeks to spin out multiple Xbox developers. Bloomberg reports that Ubisoft – which, like Arkane, is based in France – placed an offer in undisclosed and early-stage negotiations. Other Xbox studios, like Psychonauts 2 maker Double Fine, have gone independent post-Xbox as Microsoft brute forces a "reset" plan under new leadership. Two agreements to save Hellblade developer Ninja Theory fell through , and in September, Arkane's future was also looking uncertain. Last month, in a move that sure seems to align with today's report, Xbox announced an extension to the deadline to "explore options" for Arkane's future. Conflicting reports make it difficult to estimate how much work still needs to be done on Blade, which has occupied Arkane for years, including the years after Xbox closed down Arkane Austin following the Redfall disaster. Whether it's almost finished or still needs a year of work, Blade will need new backing, which is where this deal comes in. Ubisoft would be a curious home for Arkane, though you could point to shared stealth action DNA between Dishonored and Assassin's Creed. And again, they're also both French, which is especially relevant concerning labor laws. However, much like Microsoft, Ubisoft has a reputation for shuttering a lot of teams and cancelling a lot of games , though you'll hardly find a large publisher with a squeaky-clean graveyard these days. Ubisoft is also going through its own reset following several disappointing years, with a new subsidiary dedicated to pillar franchises like Assassin's Creed propped up with backing from Tencent . By some miracle, this reset has not yet seen the end of Beyond Good & Evil 2, which – not to be outdone by the misguided Dragon Age: The Veilguard pivots that certainly contributed to the end of BioWare – Ubisoft apparently wanted to be a live service game at one point. sources.title: Ubisoft reportedly wants to buy Arkane from Xbox
sources.text: There might be hope for Arkane after all: A new report says multiple companies have made offers for it. A new report from Bloomberg says Dishonored developer Arkane might not be as doomed as it appeared last month, as multiple companies have made offers to acquire the studio. Citing "people familiar with the negotiations," the Bloomberg report says Ubisoft is among Arkane's suitors, as are at least two other unnamed gaming companies. Xbox has also considered selling the studio to its own management, effectively making it independent, although whether that option is still on the table isn't clear. Despite producing an enviable slate of acclaimed immersive sims over the years (until it was compelled by senior leadership to do otherwise ), Arkane fell victim to the Xbox "reset" in July that saw thousands of employees laid off (with more still awaiting their fates) and four studios cast adrift. Arkane avoided being the fifth, reportedly thanks to France's "Florange Law" that compelled Xbox to search for a buyer before pulling the plug. The deadline for that search was November 13, after which Arkane would be shuttered—but a few weeks ahead of that date, Microsoft extended it by a month , to "explore options, including finding a partner to support the studio through the development work still ahead," a reference to the Marvel's Blade game Arkane currently has in development. That extension suggested there was at least some hope that Arkane might find a new home, instead of being closed. Going from Xbox to Ubisoft could be viewed as a "frying pan to fire" move, given Ubisoft's own ongoing financial struggles, layoffs, and closures . But Arkane's immersive sim expertise could be a good fit for some of Ubisoft's biggest properties, including Assassin's Creed, Far Cry, and—yes, I'm just going to say it—Splinter Cell, which would be magnificent in the style of Dishonored. Arkane and Ubisoft both being French companies can't hurt, either. sources.title: Nintendo Reveals the Changes It Made to The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time's Notoriously Difficult Water Temple for the Remake
sources.text: Nintendo has discussed the changes it has made to the notoriously difficult Water Temple for The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake. In an interview with Zelda boss Eiji Aonuma, Production Group No.3’s HokWai Ng, and other members of the development team published on the Nintendo website , changes made to dungeons were outlined. Crucially, Aonuma — who worked on the original Ocarina of Time back in the ‘90s — was able to finally get to what he called “overdue homework” on the Water Temple. The original Water Temple in the 1998 N64 masterpiece is infamous for its complex puzzle solving, but also its lack of handholding. This made it a bewildering challenge for many players of the original game. As someone who played Ocarina of Time back in the day — and without the help of a guide — I found the Water Temple pretty frustrating. It took me longer to work out than pretty much any part of the game, as I struggled to make sense of the water levels and locked doors. And don’t get me started on that item toggling. Ng said that Nintendo’s approach with the remake was to retain the dungeon mechanisms from the original game, but improve “playability.” “For example, we placed objects in such a way that players intuitively figure out which direction to go,” he said. “So if you look closely, you may notice areas where the layout differs slightly from the original game.” For Aonuma, the Water Temple was personal. “I wanted to do something about the Water Temple I created 28 years ago,” he said, laughing. “Since it became well known for its difficulty in the original game, I had the team make some adjustments in this version. When I designed the Water Temple all those years ago, I wanted to create an experience where simply being underwater was fun. It was a time when there were very few 3D games that even let players go underwater. I enjoy freediving, and what I find fascinating about being underwater is how different everything feels. The sounds change, and it feels like you’re in a completely different space. I wanted to create a place where players could experience those sensations. “However, with the dungeon’s complex structure and a lot of item toggling involved, you often had to open the menu screen repeatedly, making it hard to keep track of where you were and which way you were facing. We addressed those issues in this version.” To that end, the remake makes item toggling “much easier,” and Nintendo has “changed some of the walls that made it easy to lose your sense of direction to lattice-style structures, making it possible to see the rooms beyond them and get a better sense of the overall space.” Essentially, rather than simply changing the structure to make things easier, Nintendo came up with various ideas to rework it so that players wouldn’t get lost. As IGN’s Logan Plant spotted while viewing Ocarina of Time remake gameplay , the 3DS version’s wall lights, which helped guide players to water-shifting spots, return for the Switch 2 remake. And, as teased by Nintendo today, Link can instantly take off his iron boots without having to pause and go to the equipment menu. There’s a fun exchange at the end of the interview that taps into the immense nostalgia fans have for Ocarina of Time, and what I imagine will be a typical household experience when the remake comes out. “More than anything, I personally would be happy if it became a conversation starter that encourages players of different generations to share memories with each other,” Ng said. “You know, your Dad got stuck in the Water Temple plenty of times back in the day [laughs].” Aonuma: “Then kids playing this version might say, ‘Come on, it’s not that hard.’ Poor old Dad might end up feeling deflated.” While you wait for the game to come out, check out a special episode of Nintendo Voice Chat where we dive deeper into our Zelda preview. Meanwhile, we finally have confirmation of who actually developed the Ocarina of Time remake , and a roundup of the Ocarina of Time remake global release times . Wesley is IGN's Managing Editor. sources.text: A Nintendo explicou os motivos que levaram à criação do remake de The Legend of Zelda : Ocarina of Time para o Nintendo Switch 2 . Segundo Eiji Aonuma, produtor da franquia, o projeto vai além das comemorações dos 40 anos de The Legend of Zelda , celebrados em 2026. Em entrevista publicada no site oficial da Nintendo, Aonuma revelou que a decisão também está relacionada à evolução da própria equipe de desenvolvimento. Muitos profissionais que atualmente trabalham na franquia participaram apenas dos jogos mais recentes, como Breath of the Wild e Tears of the Kingdom . A proposta é permitir que esses desenvolvedores revisitem a estrutura de Ocarina of Time , lançado originalmente em 1998 para Nintendo 64, e compreendam sua importância para a identidade da série. De acordo com Aonuma, reconstruir Ocarina of Time oferece à equipe uma oportunidade de estudar decisões de design que ajudaram a definir a franquia. O produtor acredita que revisitar o desenvolvimento do clássico pode gerar novas ideias para os futuros jogos de The Legend of Zelda . A intenção não é necessariamente abandonar a liberdade dos títulos mais recentes, mas compreender como elementos tradicionais, como progressão narrativa, exploração e desenvolvimento gradual das habilidades do jogador, podem contribuir para novas experiências. Outro objetivo do remake é aproximar jogadores que conheceram a franquia por meio de Breath of the Wild da estrutura tradicional de Zelda . Enquanto os títulos mais recentes permitem explorar o mundo e escolher diferentes caminhos desde o início, Ocarina of Time apresenta uma aventura com progressão mais direcionada, na qual novos locais, habilidades e acontecimentos são introduzidos gradualmente. Para Aonuma, essa diferença representa uma oportunidade de mostrar outra abordagem de design que também faz parte da história da franquia. O remake de The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time chega em 5 de novembro de 2026 , exclusivamente para Nintendo Switch 2, como parte das comemorações do aniversário de 40 anos da série. sources.title: Nintendo explains why Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake’s auto jump was hard to drop
sources.text: A simple decision to let players jump whenever they wanted has big implications for Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake The decision to drop Link’s auto-jump from Zelda: Ocarina of Time’s Nintendo Switch 2 remake was not a simple one, Nintendo has revealed. In a new blog post explaining some of the creative decisions made in the upcoming remake, the game’s developers discuss the issues that arose when trying to modernize Ocarina of Time’s control scheme. The most significant change, they explained, is allowing the player to jump on command, rather than auto-jump kicking in towards a ledge, something which then influenced how the rest of the game was designed. Longtime Zelda producer Eiji Aonuma said that the original game’s auto-jump was a “convenient” design decision, as it meant that the developers had more control over where players could explore. There were restrictions in place, and the environments were designed around this. “If you remove that restriction and make it possible to jump anywhere, you need to anticipate all kinds of player behavior and make corresponding adjustments to the environment,” Aonuma explains. “So at first, we were like, ‘Are we sure about this?’ So, even a single change can instantly increase the number of things that need to be reviewed.” On top of this, Young Link and Adult Link have different jumping distances, so developers had to be mindful that players were always able to pull off leaps regardless of who they were playing as. It is, therefore, no surprise then that the developers have also made changes to the dungeons, since getting rid of the auto-jump opens up many more possibilities. In particular, Aonuma admitted that there have been changes made to the infamous Water Temple, based on years of complaints that it was too difficult. “When I designed the Water Temple all those years ago, I wanted to create an experience where simply being underwater was fun,” Aonuma said. “It was a time when there were very few 3D games that even let players go underwater. “However, with the dungeonâs complex structure and a lot of item toggling involved, you often had to open the menu screen repeatedly, making it hard to keep track of where you were and which way you were facing. We addressed those issues in this version.” More specifically, it’s claimed that players will have better visibility in the new Water Temple, so we won’t get as lost. It should also be easier to toggle between items that we need to traverse the dungeon. That said, Aonuma insisted on keeping some of the original design quirks in the remake. He said that he struggled to adapt to the new Jump Attack, which is now a two-button input. Due to this, players can toggle the controls to make it a single-button input, like in the original release. Aonuma has also stated previously that he is “surprised” that the team did not make more changes in the remake, so it sounds like we are in for a faithful recreation of the original experience.

sources.title: OG Zelda: Ocarina of Time dev responsible for the infamous water temple used the remake to atone
sources.text: 15 years after remaking the game for 3DS purely to "do something about the water temple" Zelda series lead Eiji Aonuma has admitted that he wanted to use The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake to make the Water Temple a bit less obtuse. In the 28 years since The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, one challenge has lived in infamy: the dreaded Water Temple. While the classic adventure game was universally praised, the Water Temple was the sole sticking point for many, with its somewhat obtuse design proving a huge challenge. However, to many people – myself included – the problem with the Water Temple was less about the challenge or dungeon design itself and more about the tedium of constantly pausing to equip or remove the Iron Boots to navigate the area. As for The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake, Aonuma – whose role in the N64 classic was as the game's dungeon designer – explained that the Water Temple was a big motivator in Nintendo's Ask the Developer article about the game. "I had some overdue homework: I wanted to do something about the Water Temple I created 28 years ago," Aonuma says, explaining, "Since it became well known for its difficulty in the original game, I had the team make some adjustments in this version." However, this is not the first time Aonuma spoke about wanting to change the Water Temple; in fact, in a 2011 Iwata Asks interview , Aonuma said, "I wanted to do something about the Water Temple" when discussing his motivation for making The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time 3D. He explained at the time, "Everyone talks about it, so it’s been a longstanding wish of mine these 13 years!" but clearly its version of the dreaded dungeon wasn't enough. "When I designed the Water Temple all those years ago, I wanted to create an experience where simply being underwater was fun," Aonuma explains in 2026. He cites his love of freediving and finds it fascinating "how different everything feels" when you are submerged. "I wanted to create a place where players could experience those sensations," Aonuma explains. The remake's director, HokWai Ng, explains that the remake makes item toggling easier, as well as changing "some of the walls that made it easy to lose your sense of direction to lattice-style structures," so hopefully this new version will finally satisfy Aonuma's desire to "fix" the temple. sources.text: A Bethesda finalmente revelou uma das informações mais aguardadas pelos fãs de RPG: o nome oficial de The Elder Scrolls 6. O próximo capítulo da franquia será chamado The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel e ganhou seu primeiro logo oficial em um vídeo especial publicado nesta terça-feira (3), durante as comemorações de 40 anos da Bethesda Game Studios. A revelação foi feita por Todd Howard, produtor executivo e uma das principais figuras da desenvolvedora. No vídeo comemorativo, o executivo relembra a trajetória do estúdio e comenta a relação dos jogadores com seus games antes de anunciar que a ocasião seria perfeita para revelar como o novo The Elder Scrolls realmente se chama. Apesar da novidade, a Bethesda não apresentou imagens de gameplay, detalhes da história ou uma previsão de lançamento. Em uma publicação separada, a empresa também alertou que “ainda vai demorar algum tempo” até estar pronta para compartilhar mais informações sobre o projeto. O nome Sentinel já era alvo de rumores e especulações há algum tempo. A escolha também reforça teorias da comunidade de que o próximo RPG da Bethesda será ambientado em Hammerfell, uma das províncias do continente de Tamriel. Sentinel é uma cidade localizada no noroeste de Hammerfell, próxima à Baía de Iliac, região que separa as províncias de Hammerfell e High Rock. O território já apareceu em outros jogos da franquia, incluindo The Elder Scrolls II: Daggerfall, The Elder Scrolls Online e The Elder Scrolls Adventures: Redguard. A região também é mencionada em uma citação trazida no fim do teaser apresentado pela Bethesda. O texto em questão diz o seguinte, na tradução para o português brasileiro: “O pergaminho revelou apenas um vislumbre, um véu sutilmente erguido diante dos meus olhos. Um futuro perdido. Uma vitória desfeita. Areias do tempo espalhadas pelo destino.” — Yazar, Sacerdote das Mariposas da Alta Rainha Iradne de Hammerfell (4ª Era, ano 206). A possibilidade de explorar essa região também alimenta teorias sobre a presença de mecânicas inéditas na série. No mês passado, Bruce Nesmith, ex-desenvolvedor da Bethesda e designer principal de Skyrim, comentou que gostaria de ver os rumores sobre a ambientação se confirmarem. Segundo ele, o cenário poderia abrir espaço para a utilização de barcos e exploração marítima, algo que ainda não teve grande destaque na franquia. A confirmação do subtítulo chega após uma espera considerável dos fãs. The Elder Scrolls VI foi anunciado originalmente em 2018, durante a E3, mas a Bethesda praticamente não compartilhou novidades concretas sobre o projeto desde então. Na semana passada, uma reportagem do The Verge indicou que a desenvolvedora poderia revelar o nome do jogo ainda em novembro. A expectativa era de que o anúncio acontecesse próximo ao aniversário de 15 anos de The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim, lançado originalmente em 11 de novembro de 2011. Outro detalhe curioso surgiu em uma publicação recente de Asha Sharma, CEO do Xbox. Ao comentar uma demonstração de The Elder Scrolls VI que teria recebido durante o verão no hemisfério norte, a executiva utilizou oito asteriscos para esconder o subtítulo do jogo — exatamente a quantidade de letras de Sentinel. Por enquanto, a Bethesda mantém o mistério sobre os próximos passos do RPG. Considerando o longo período desde o anúncio original e a falta de informações sobre o desenvolvimento, ainda não há previsão oficial de lançamento ou confirmação de plataformas além do ecossistema Xbox e PC. A possibilidade de uma versão para PlayStation também segue sem resposta. Enquanto isso, a empresa destacou que Skyrim continua sendo o jogo mais jogado da história da Bethesda Game Studios, considerando o total de jogadores ao longo de sua trajetória. O novo capítulo terá a difícil missão de suceder um dos RPGs mais populares de todos os tempos, além de atender as expectativas dos fãs que esperam pelo novo jogo há anos. sources.text: From grappling mutants to cyborg tanks, discover which kaiju is right for you. With its giant-sized fanbase, Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered has plenty of players ready to get tooth, nail, and claw stuck into its PlayStation 5 release on November 3. Although it would be understandable that newcomers might feel a little intimidated choosing between 12 world crushing kaiju, each with their own stats, moveset, and special abilities. Never fear – we have the rundown on which colossus matches your playstyle to ensure you’re the true king of the monsters. Ideal for: Players who want to dive straight in. The face which sank a thousand ships. Godzilla is the iconic kaiju who all other kaiju want to be, beat, or be friends with. As the game’s default character, the giant lizard is balanced for newbies and veterans alike, with a high amount of starting health and decent all-round stats. Godzilla also possesses a tail useful enough for a mighty wake-up strike when he’s downed, and some fairly swift claws, so many of his melee combos are effective for beginners. But don’t rely too much on his high-energy pulse – while it’s formidable, the slow charge leaves him open to counters. Similarly, ranged attackers can take advantage of his relatively sluggish projectiles, so close that distance or you’ll be heading back to Monster Island with your giant tail between your legs. Ideal for: Players annoyed at their friend for picking Heisei Godzilla. In terms of film history, Godzilla 2000 is a more modern incarnation of the legendary lizard, reflecting a new era for the new millennium. Although he’s arguably a slightly more vulnerable version of his Heisei predecessor. As a result, while Godzilla 2000 is a bit faster than his kaiju shoto fighter twin, he’s not quite as strong. He’s still fairly well balanced and arguably easier to use than Heisei, so makes for a solid alternative. And his distinctive purple dorsal plates look pretty cool, too. Ideal for: Players who want to control the battlefield. There’s a reason why this fearsome three-headed beast is seen as Godzilla’s archnemesis. Giant wings, gravity beams, and a desire to annihilate humanity, the threat of King Ghidorah should never be taken lightly. Given his monstrous size it shouldn’t be a surprise that the ‘supreme ruler of the cosmos’ isn’t the fastest kaiju on the block, but he’s resilient and a perfect ‘zoning’ character, capable of keeping foes at a distance with a variety of projectiles. His flight is a little limited due to its energy drain, but it’s balanced by a lightning blast that has no charge while airborne. However, despite his colossal wings, Ghidorah’s lack of arms and stubby legs makes him a poor melee fighter. Ideal for: Players who think defense is the best offense. He might look a bit like Godzooky with more spikes, but mutant dinosaur Anguirus is one of Godzilla’s most loyal allies – even if his track record against other kaiju hasn’t been the best in the movies. The Monster Island citizen is fast and aggressive, but his low power and lack of long-range attacks means Anguirus is best utilized as a counter-attack specialist. His block might be on the slow side due to its turning animation, but it actually damages an attacking opponent due to Anguirus’ rear spines. With his high defense and solid grappling skills, this mutant shouldn’t be underestimated. Ideal for: Players who love to hit and run. Given its status as a guardian to the ancient underground civilisation of Seatopia, Megalon is more of an antagonist than an out-and-out villain in Godzilla lore. While not quite as domineering as its colossal rivals, the subterranean kaiju is still capable of putting a hurt on with its drill-like appendages. Megalon’s primary advantage is its tunnelling skill which not only allows it to avoid attacks, but also pop-up and grab opponents. Even though burrowing uses energy, it still makes Megalon a difficult fighter to pin down, especially when used in tandem with its myriad of electricity attacks. On the flip side, Megalon isn’t the most durable of beasts with below average defense. Stick and move, or die. Ideal for: Players wanting to attack with deadly speed. One of the most sadistic fighters to hail from M Space Hunter Nebula, cyborg kaiju Gigan is easily one of Godzilla’s more vicious adversaries. Despite being defeated multiple times, the hook-clawed Gigan just keeps coming back for more. Unsurprisingly, Gigan’s tenacious approach makes him perfect for aggressive rushdown tactics. He’s not only swift, but his teleportation ability gives him incredible range and evasion skills. And those hooks aren’t for decoration either, delivering damage-heavy edged strikes. His Laser Eye is a little unwieldy, and he’s vulnerable to energy attacks, but Gigan remains a versatile option for anyone wanting a decent melee and range mix-up. Ideal for: Players wanting a classic tank character. Known as ‘death incarnate’, everything about Destoroyah is built to intimidate. Giant wings, clawed hands, taloned feet… this mutant crustacean almost has it all. Which is to say, Destoroyah is one of the more powerful creatures in the game with brutal physical assaults and a wide variety of high-damage – and often unblockable – energy attacks that truly make him the perfect mid-range monster. But there’s a cost. Destoroyah’s best abilities are extremely power hungry, so without them he’s potentially ineffective given how painfully slow his movement is. Ideal for: Players wanting speed above all else. With his dominance of the skies and fearsome pteranodon looks, you’d be fooled into thinking Rodan is an out-and-out villain, but he’s more a force of chaos, even capable of being selfless in some parts of Godzilla lore. sources.text: Lançamentos de games em NOVEMBRO de 2026 - Calendário VOXL Além do aguardado GTA 6, novembro traz remake de Ocarina of Time e mais de 30 jogos. Confira as estreias do mês. Crédito: Voxl Sempre fui um grande fã de kaijus e de toda essa cultura de criaturas e robôs gigantes. Por isso, quando soube que Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee receberia uma versão remasterizada, fiquei bastante empolgado. Sempre tive vontade de jogar esse clássico, lançado originalmente em 2002 para Nintendo GameCube e Xbox, mas nunca tive acesso às plataformas necessárias na época. Agora, mais de duas décadas depois, finalmente tenho a oportunidade de conhecer esse jogo em uma versão voltada para os consoles e computadores atuais. Com a chegada de Godzilla Minus Zero , sequência de Godzilla Minus One prevista para novembro de 2026, o momento também parece propício para resgatar um clássico da porradaria entre monstros gigantes. Afinal, Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee tem aquela energia dos jogos que você reúne os primos para jogar, sem compromisso com o realismo ou com uma narrativa complexa, apenas para trocar golpes, destruir cenários e dar boas risadas. É um tipo de diversão descompromissada que não se leva tão a sério — e isso faz parte do seu charme. Desenvolvido originalmente pela Pipeworks Studios, o jogo coloca kaijus conhecidos da franquia em confrontos nos quais prédios e outros elementos do cenário também fazem parte da pancadaria. A versão remasterizada busca preservar essa experiência, atualizando a apresentação visual e levando o combate para plataformas modernas, além de incluir recursos como partidas online. Mas, quando um jogo clássico retorna depois de tantos anos, surge uma questão importante: por que modernizar apenas os gráficos e os recursos técnicos? Relançamentos também são oportunidades para rever aspectos da experiência que vão além da resolução das imagens ou do desempenho. Controles mais flexíveis, opções gráficas ajustáveis e recursos de acessibilidade podem fazer a diferença para que mais pessoas consigam aproveitar um jogo. Isso é especialmente relevante em títulos de ação, nos quais acompanhar vários personagens na tela, identificar ataques em meio a explosões, interpretar informações da interface e executar comandos no momento certo pode representar uma barreira para jogadores com deficiência. É com essa perspectiva que analiso Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered . Além de revisitar um clássico que sempre tive vontade de experimentar, quero entender quais recursos de acessibilidade estão disponíveis nessa nova versão, quais barreiras permanecem e até que ponto o relançamento aproveita a oportunidade de adaptar essa experiência às necessidades de jogadores com deficiência. Afinal, destruir cidades com monstros gigantes pode ser uma diversão para muita gente, mas essa diversão só será realmente acessível quando mais jogadores puderem participar dela. Vale ressaltar que a acessibilidade é uma experiência individual e se aplica de maneira diferente a cada pessoa, de acordo com suas necessidades e características. Portanto, as impressões apresentadas nesta análise partem da minha experiência pessoal como pessoa com baixa visão. Meu objetivo é destacar os recursos de acessibilidade presentes no jogo, explicar como eles podem contribuir para uma experiência mais inclusiva e apontar as barreiras que encontrei durante os testes. Essas observações não pretendem representar a experiência de todas as pessoas com deficiência, mas contribuir para que mais jogadores conheçam as possibilidades e limitações oferecidas pelo título. Aviso de transparência: Esta análise foi realizada com uma chave de acesso antecipado disponibilizada pela equipe de Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered para PS5, antes do lançamento oficial do jogo. O título é desenvolvido pela Pipeworks Studios e publicado pela Atari. Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered oferece legendas, mas não permite alterar o tamanho ou personalizar sua apresentação. Também não há opções de legendas ocultas ( closed captions ) que identifiquem sons importantes do ambiente e dos combates, o que pode dificultar o acompanhamento das partidas por jogadores surdos ou com deficiência auditiva. Um dos pontos mais decepcionantes é a falta de opções para personalizar os controles. Mesmo sendo um relançamento para plataformas modernas, Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered não oferece remapeamento de comandos nem ajustes mais detalhados para adaptar a jogabilidade às necessidades de cada pessoa. Essa limitação pesa especialmente em um jogo de luta e ação no qual é necessário executar diferentes comandos durante confrontos movimentados. Sem a possibilidade de reorganizar os botões, jogadores com deficiência motora podem encontrar dificuldades para realizar determinadas ações ou simplesmente não conseguir configurar os comandos de uma maneira confortável. A ausência de alternativas também reduz a flexibilidade para quem precisa de uma configuração específica por questões de mobilidade ou coordenação. É frustrante que uma versão remasterizada não aproveite a oportunidade para incluir recursos tão importantes. Atualizar os gráficos e levar o jogo a plataformas atuais não é suficiente para modernizar a experiência quando os controles continuam sem opções básicas de personalização. A vibração do controle pode ser ativada ou desativada, mas esse ajuste pontual está longe de compensar a falta de remapeamento. Nas configurações de áudio, o jogo permite ajustar separadamente o volume da música, dos efeitos sonoros e das vozes dos personagens. Essa divisão oferece algum controle sobre a mixagem, mas não é acompanhada de recursos específicos que ajudem jogadores com deficiência auditiva a identificar os acontecimentos durante as partidas. O título não apresenta indicadores visuais para sons relevantes, que poderiam ajudar a sinalizar ataques e outros eventos importantes. Em meio à destruição dos cenários e à movimenta

sources.name: Eurogamer
sources.title: "We're doing great," says id Software boss, despite losing "about half of our studio" amid devastating Xbox cuts
sources.text: Iconic Doom and Quake developer id Software was among the most heavily impacted Microsoft-owned studios during Xbox CEO Asha Sharma's devastating business "reset" earlier this year, with around 136 employees reportedly losing their jobs. In the wake of those layoffs, id Software co-studio director Marty Stratton was recently asked about the current state of the developer, and how it has been affected by Sharma's cuts. "We're doing great," Stratton told journalists at a recent event (via IGN ). "Not to handwave the [layoffs] away… everybody knows we had about half of our studio exit as part of that," he continued. "But there was a very deliberate effort to make sure that we were incredibly viable coming out of that across everything we do, across game development and technology department." This is not the first time a senior id Software member has pushed back on the narrative the studio has been "nerfed into the ground and gutted" . Hugo Martin, id's other co-studio head previously claimed the remaining team is "the size we were when we made Doom 2016, and id Tech is very much alive and well". Sharma's Xbox reset will ultimately see 3,200 jobs cut across Microsoft's gaming division, with many of those still to come. Those impacted by the first wave of cuts in July, however, included developers working on the id Software's id Tech engine. This is the engine behind all of the studio's games, and is known to be among the most performant engines, consistently producing visually-impressive games that require modest specs to run. Following the layoffs, many inside and outside the studio said the id Tech team had been gutted. Longtime id Software programmer Chris Hays, who notably wasn't among those let go, said at the time , "It is hard to make a game that is triple-A, that is like we've done before, with half the people. And by hard I mean impossible". Hays also claimed "entire departments" and "entire disciplines" are gone. While Stratton hasn't addressed those comments directly, he revealed id Software is now "working more closely than ever" with MachineGames, the Swedish studio behind the modern Wolfenstein games, and Indiana Jones and the Great Circle . "We've always had a very close partnership with [MachineGames], but I think we're at a point with technology development that both teams are incredibly talented and have incredibly talented engineers and we're really on an amazing path that had started pre-[layoffs]," he explained. "We'd kicked this off earlier this year. We're really excited about that. We're both really really bullish on what we have ahead." Id Software's next project remains unclear. MachineGames, on the other hand, recently said it's not done with Wolfenstein , so it's possible a sequel to 2017's The New Colossus is in the works.

sources.title: Doom studio is "doing great" despite Xbox cutting half its staff, studio head insists
sources.text: We're still not sure what's next for either team A total of 3,200 jobs will be cut at Xbox by the end of this fiscal year as part of an extensive restructuring. One of the casualties already is id Software , which has lost somewhere in the region of half its staff. That said, if you ask current leadership, everything at the Doom and Quake studio is fine and dandy at the moment. Marty Stratton, studio co-director of id Software, commented on how the company's been doing since the layoffs hit over the summer during a preview event for Doom: The Dark Ages DLC. "We're doing great," he says, per IGN . "Not to handwave the [layoffs] away," he adds. "Everybody knows we had about half of our studio exit as part of that. But there was a very deliberate effort to make sure that we were incredibly viable coming out of that across everything we do, across game development and technology department." Being down half your team is pretty significant. Reportedly, id Tech itself, the studio's in-house engine, is now being managed by exactly one whole person . While that's certainly viable financially, I'm not sure how structurally sound that is long-term. Stratton goes on. "We're working more closely with MachineGames than ever," he states. "We've always had a very close partnership with them, but I think we're at a point with technology development that both teams are incredibly talented and have incredibly talented engineers and we're really on an amazing path that had started pre-[layoffs]." A question mark has loomed over MachineGames since the release of Indiana Jones and the Great Circle. The prevailing rumor is Wolfenstein 3, and given the general push toward established IP Xbox has been making amid all the redundancies, that seems a safe bet. But what the collaboration between the two companies looks like, and where that leaves the next Doom, are bigger questions. "We'd kicked this off earlier this year. We're really excited about that," Stratton adds. "We're both really really bullish on what we have ahead." stories.title: 'Go Play GTA 6, We Need to Detox,' Wardogs Developer Tells Fans as It Prepares to Take December Off
stories.summary: After the runaway success of Wardogs, a new sandbox multiplayer shooter in Early Access on PC, the team at Bulkhead is taking a well-deserved break. They want you to know you can take a break, too.

sources.name: IGN
sources.title: 'Go Play GTA 6, We Need to Detox,' Wardogs Developer Tells Fans as It Prepares to Take December Off
sources.text: After the runaway success of Wardogs , a new sandbox multiplayer shooter in Early Access on PC, the team at Bulkhead is taking a well-deserved break — and they want you to know you can take a break, too. It’s a break the team likely needs. Since launch, there’s been balance patch after balance patch, hotfixes, major updates, and small updates. Wardogs even saw some controversy when it attempted to region lock players to prevent cheating. Speaking to Edge Magazine, via GamesRadar , Bulkhead CEO Joe Brammer explained the pressure the team had been dealing with. "Everyone has done something that's not in their job description,” Brammer said. “Everyone wears multiple hats, because they can see the path to success with the product." Following a flurry of updates and a disappointing Wardogs Season 2 launch , Bulkhead is taking the whole month of December off to rest and refresh for the new year and the road to the game’s 1.0 launch. "We're going to make sure players know they can f**k off in December," he said. "Go play GTA 6 , we need to detox.” It’s a refreshing approach to hear a developer acknowledge the incoming leviathan that is Rockstar’s open-world crime sequel. Most publishers are just quietly changing their plans with no outward communication, but Bulkhead addressed the massive, massive elephant filling the room. GTA 6 is out on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox, and it is expected to be the biggest entertainment launch of all time. A number of publishers and developers either worked to release their games beforehand, leading to the September crunch, or push them back into early 2027. Star Citizen chief Chris Roberts claimed he delayed spinoff Squadron 42 into next year because he didn't want it going up against the "attention buzz saw of GTA 6." "While GTA 6 isn’t launching on PC this November, pretty much all outlets and most content creators will be all over it, not leaving a lot of room for other coverage," Roberts continued. Analysts expect GTA 6 will make over $5 billion in launch week alone , so expect it to fill your feeds for a few weeks. Kirk McKeand is a Contributor on IGN News. Find him on Twitter @MckKirk

sources.title: "Go play GTA 6, we need to detox": Wardogs studio Bulkhead is taking a month-long break
sources.text: The Wardogs team is planning to take a long break to celebrate the success of its early access release, and CEO Joe Brammer knows that it'll probably be fine because players will have plenty to occupy them – in the form of GTA 6 . Speaking to Edge Magazine, Brammer explains that the team has worked hard to earn the right to play hard. "Everyone has done something that's not in their job description. Everyone wears multiple hats, because they can see the path to success with the product." With the early access launch of Wardogs in the rear-view, the entirety of developer Bulkhead Studios will be taking an extended break, with leave stretching throughout the entire month of December. It's a bold strategy, but one that Brammer is quick to double-down on. "We're going to make sure players know they can fuck off in December," he says, suggesting the team does have some idea of the backlog of bug reports and balance complaints that could be waiting for them come January. The hope, clearly, is that those players will be too distracted by something else to be blasting the Bulkhead forums: "Go play GTA 6, we need to detox," Brammer says. With most games wondering how they'll hope to hold onto their audiences once Rockstar drops its nuke – and Fortnite offering near-unlimited freebies to certain lucky players – it's almost refreshing to see a team unapologetically accepting that its fans will have something else on their minds, and hoping that they'll come back once they're finished with Leonida. stories.title: GTA 6 Preload, Global Release Times and Install Size Confirmed, Rockstar Announces Physical Cover Art Poster and Map of Leonida
stories.summary: Rockstar Games has confirmed the GTA 6 preload and global release times, as well as the install size of the game.

sources.title: GTA 6 Preload, Global Release Times and Install Size Confirmed, Rockstar Announces Physical Cover Art Poster and Map of Leonida
sources.text: Rockstar Games has confirmed the GTA 6 preload and global release times as well as the install size of the game. Digital preloading on PS5 kicks off at midnight local time in your respective timezone on Tuesday, November 10, Rockstar said . On Xbox Series X and S it’s slightly different — preloading begins on Tuesday, November 10 at 12am GMT (UK time). That's 4pm PT and 7pm ET on November 9. Code-in-box versions for both consoles “should” be available from retailers beginning November 12, Rockstar added. Rockstar has also now officially confirmed that GTA 6 itself launches globally on November 19, using the local midnight release timing strategy across PS5 and Xbox Series X and S. As for the install size, Rockstar confirmed that the preload file weighs in at up to 212 GB, “depending on your device.” “So make sure you've got ample space to begin pre-loading as soon as possible,” Rockstar said. Elsewhere, Rockstar said that on November 19, the day GTA 6 comes out, it will add an official printable GTA 6 cover art poster and map of Leonida as a free digital download to the official site. A double-sided physical version of this poster will also be made available shortly after launch from the Rockstar Store — for $0.99 on its own or as a free gift with any purchase from the Rockstar Store. We’ve got plenty more on GTA 6 while you wait for its November 19 release date, including an unlikely gameplay reveal in the latest episode of South Park , how GTA 6 named one of its biggest mechanics after a beloved GTA 4 meme , and how GTA 6's map will open up relatively early and let you explore freely . sources.text: You can start preloading GTA 6 from November 10, and these are the details you need to know The GTA 6 preload time is almost here, taking us a huge step closer to finally exploring Leonida with Jason and Lucia. sources.text: Grand Theft Auto 6 Grand Theft Auto VI GTA 6 Pre-Load We’re just over two weeks out from the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6 and Rockstar Games has finally revealed all of the details people need to know about getting the digital-only open-world game installed on their gaming console of choice. The studio also confirmed that, yes, GTA 6 has a whopping 212GB install size , so start making room for that and god help you if you have an Xbox Series S. Here’s everything you need to know about getting GTA 6 ready to play for its release on November 19, 2026. Digital pre-loading on PlayStation 5 will start globally on Tuesday, November 10 at midnight local time. On Xbox Series X|S, pre-loading begins globally on Tuesday, November 10 at 12 a.m. GMT, which is 7:00 p.m. ET on the previous day, November 9. If you pre-order GTA 6 digitally, you’ll have access to pre-load the game immediately. If you are waiting for one of the codes in a box to ship to your home or be picked up in store, those will become available starting November 12. You’ll be able to take that code, redeem it, and immediately start pre-loading the game. That’s a big file size, and console servers are going to get hammered when everyone starts trying to download it at once. To put it in perspective, 212GB is roughly one third of the available storage on a base PS5 and roughly a quarter of the available storage on a 1TB model. On Xbox Series S, it’s closer to half. In addition to taking some time depending on the speed of your internet, you’ll want to make sure you have your library cleared of any non-essential games. Good luck to you if you have children who are constantly swapping between a dozen different games every day. The global release times for when GTA 6 goes live were previously announced, and unfortunately the U.S. is one of the last time zones to get access to the game. Yes, the game will have been out in some parts of the world for roughly 18 hours by the time GTA 6 goes live stateside. My advice is to just stay logged out that day. sources.title: Grand Theft Auto bonus that used to be free with every physical game is now a $1 purchase for GTA 6
sources.text: You won't be getting your Leonida map in the box here Once upon a time, Grand Theft Auto 3, Vice City, and San Andreas featured fold-out posters in the box, with a map on one side and game art on the other. GTA 4 and 5 used double-sided maps, showing each game's locations at increasing levels of detail on each side. Rockstar is keeping the tradition alive with GTA 6 , but as the studio moves to abandon physical media , you're gonna have to get it separately. "On November 19 we will be adding an official printable Grand Theft Auto VI cover art poster and map of Leonida as a free digital download to the official site," Rockstar says in an announcement also offering GTA 6 pre-load details . "A double-sided physical version of this poster will also be made available shortly after launch from the Rockstar Store – for $0.99 on its own or as a free gift with any purchase from the Rockstar Store." I guess the promise of getting it as "a free gift" means Rockstar technically isn't charging extra for the map, but you'll still have to spend extra money on merch to get hold of it. It's not actually included with the game itself. The "code-in-box" versions of GTA 6 will be available starting November 12, and Rockstar makes no mention of this map being available inside that package. If you really wanted to get the map for free with the game, you could wait until "shortly after launch" when it's available from the Rockstar Store, then buy the code-in-box version and get the map as a free gift then. The catch is that Rockstar describes the code-in-box version as being available "while supplies last," so there's no guarantee it'll still be available past the pre-order window. Bummer. I suppose I'm at least glad that Rockstar is paying tribute to the map pack-ins it used to include with its games, but the hoops we've now gotta go through to get these bonuses are a sad reminder of what we're losing while publishers attempt to usher in the death of physical media.
